metadata.selection_criteria: General-purpose + paid-data marketplaces from focus list of 10
metadata.excluded: Datarade (aggregator), Kaggle (free), Hugging Face (free), Nasdaq Data Link (finance-niche), Google Dataset Search (meta-search)

findings.title: Comparative Summary
findings.summary: Side-by-side comparison of all 5 qualifying marketplaces across key provider dimensions.
findings.details:
Platform Fee:
  AWS Data Exchange      3% public; 1.5–3% private (tiered)
  Snowflake Marketplace  0% (currently)
  Databricks Marketplace 0%
  Google Analytics Hub   2–3% (tiered)
  Narrative.io           0% from seller (25% charged to buyer)

Payment Mechanism:
  AWS        → AWS disburses monthly
  Snowflake  → Stripe (or Snowflake for MCD)
  Databricks → None — offline billing by provider
  Google     → Google pays ~21st of month
  Narrative  → Narrative billing system

Approval Timeline:
  AWS        → Undefined (manual review)
  Snowflake  → ~1 day profile; paid = vetting call
  Databricks → Partner review (days–weeks)
  Google     → 2–4 weeks for commercial
  Narrative  → Self-service, no gate

Exclusivity: NONE on any platform — multi-marketplace strategy fully viable.

findings.title: AWS Data Exchange
findings.summary: 3% fee on public offers (1.5–3% on private, tiered by deal size). Monthly disbursement after AWS collects. Subscription pricing 1–36 months. Undefined approval timeline.
findings.details:
PAYMENT TERMS
• Public offers: 3% listing fee on pre-tax TCV
• Private offers: <$1M = 3%, $1–10M = 2%, >$10M = 1.5%, renewals = 1.5%
• BYOS (Bring Your Own Subscription): 0%
• Disbursement: monthly rolling, net of fees, only after subscriber pays
• Currency: USD only
• Pricing: subscription-based (1–36 months, up to 5 combos). No metered/one-time model.
• Refunds: provider-controlled, must approve each request
• Infra costs: $0.04/grant/hour, S3 storage $0.023/GB/month, API Gateway fees

APPROVAL PROCESS
• Must be AWS customer in good standing
• Eligible jurisdictions: ~16 countries (US, EU, UK, AU, JP, IN, etc.)
• Register on Marketplace Portal, complete tax (W-9/W-8) + banking
• Submit qualification request via AWS Support case
• AWS team conducts detailed review — timeline NOT published
• Account is permanently locked to provider identity

EASE OF PUBLISHING
• Any file format (Parquet recommended). Also REST APIs, Redshift datashares, S3 direct, Lake Formation
• Console GUI + Catalog API + Data Exchange API + CLI — full automation support
• Workflow: create dataset → revision → import assets → finalize → publish
• New revisions auto-publish to subscribers
• Optional subscription verification (required for PII products)

OTHER TERMS
• No exclusivity
• No PII by default; Extended Provider Program for sensitive data
• Must respond to API subscriber questions within 1 business day
• All datasets in a product must be same AWS Region
• Provider feedback: limited organic traffic, limited seller analytics

findings.title: Snowflake Marketplace
findings.summary: 0% platform fee (currently). Stripe-based payments. Usage, subscription, and installment pricing. ~1 day approval for free listings; paid requires go-to-market vetting.
findings.details:
PAYMENT TERMS
• Platform fee: 0% — Snowflake monetizes via consumer compute, not commission
• Legal terms reserve right to introduce fees in future
• Payment via Stripe Express (new account required; can't reuse existing)
• MCD program: consumers use existing Snowflake credits to buy listings (US-to-US only)
• Pricing models:
  – Usage-based: per-query, monthly base, billable events (with monthly cap)
  – Subscription: 1–36 months, recurring or non-recurring
  – Installment: periodic payments with optional skip periods
• All costs non-cancelable and non-refundable

APPROVAL PROCESS
• Full Snowflake account required (no trials). ACCOUNTADMIN role needed.
• Accept Provider and Consumer Terms
• Profile review: ~1 business day
• Free listing review: ~1 business day
• Paid listings: must demonstrate "go-to-market readiness"
  – Partners with Snowflake Partner Manager: engage them first
  – Others: submit case, potential vetting call. Approval at Snowflake's discretion.
• Stripe Express setup required. 19 approved billing countries.
• Max 100 listings per provider

EASE OF PUBLISHING
• Product types: Secure Share (tables/views — simplest), Native App, Connected App
• Tooling: Snowsight/Provider Studio GUI, SQL API (CREATE LISTING), notebooks
• Required: data dictionary (mandatory), SQL examples, business domain email, logo
• Free listing effort: low–medium. Paid: medium–high.

OTHER TERMS
• No exclusivity
• Respond to consumer inquiries within 3 business days
• No sensitive personal data in public listings
• One provider profile per legal entity
• AI products must disclose LLM model, logic, guardrails

findings.title: Databricks Marketplace
findings.summary: 0% platform fee. No built-in payment processing — all billing handled offline by provider. Partner program approval required (days–weeks).
findings.details:
PAYMENT TERMS
• Platform fee: 0% — no revenue share, listing fee, or transaction fee
• No built-in payment processing whatsoever
• All transactions happen offline: provider negotiates, invoices, collects independently
• After payment settled, provider clicks "Fulfill" to provision access via Delta Sharing
• Implication: great margins, but must build/use own billing infrastructure

APPROVAL PROCESS
• Public Marketplace: apply through Databricks Data Partner Program
  – Manual review, no published SLA (expect days to weeks)
  – Requires Databricks Premium workspace with Unity Catalog
• Private Exchange: self-service, no approval needed (invite-only visibility)

EASE OF PUBLISHING
• Asset types: Delta Lake tables, views, volumes (files), ML models, notebooks, Git repos, apps, MCP servers
• Only tables accessible to non-Databricks consumers (via open Delta Sharing protocol)
• Provider Console GUI for creating shares and listings
• If already on Databricks: low effort (minutes to hours)
• If NOT on Databricks: moderate–high (provision workspace, Unity Catalog, Delta Lake setup)

OTHER TERMS
• No exclusivity
• No sensitive personal data allowed, ever
• 30-day minimum notice before discontinuing a product
• Response SLAs: 3 business days (access), 5 business days (other)
• Must update at "most frequent logical refresh rate"
• One provider profile per org
• No geographic restrictions
• Scale: ~230+ providers, ~2,200+ listings (mid-2024)

findings.title: Google Cloud Analytics Hub (BigQuery Sharing)
findings.summary: 2–3% fee (tiered, via Cloud Marketplace). Monthly payout ~21st. Free listings trivial; commercial requires Partner Advantage + 2–4 week review.
findings.details:
PAYMENT TERMS
• Revenue share (April 2025 Vendor Net Revenue Schedule):
  – Standard/small: 3%
  – New deals: 2%
  – $1–10M TCV: 2%
  – Renewals: 1.5%
  – >$10M TCV: 1.5%
• Disbursement: ~21st of each month, aggregated across all customers
• Prices in USD; customers pay in 30+ currencies across 65 countries
• Pricing: free (subscriber pays own compute), paid subscription (monthly auto-renew), trial, custom private offers

APPROVAL PROCESS
• Free/private listings: no formal approval. Enable API, grant Publisher role, publish.
• Commercial Marketplace listings:
  – Join Google Partner Advantage program
  – Must be incorporated in eligible jurisdiction (65+ countries)
  – Product must be production-ready and enterprise-ready
  – Onboarding via Partner Hub + Producer Portal
  – Review: 2–5 business days, up to 2 weeks. Total: plan 2–4 weeks.

EASE OF PUBLISHING
• Supported: BigQuery datasets, views, ML models, UDFs, stored procedures, Pub/Sub topics (streaming)
• Tooling: Console GUI, REST API, gcloud CLI, Terraform/Pulumi, Python SDK, Producer Portal
• Free listing: under an hour
• Commercial listing: significantly more (Partner Advantage, payment profile, tax docs, review cycles)

OTHER TERMS
• No exclusivity (but feature-parity required vs. other channels)
• Data egress controls: can restrict copying/exporting/cloning
• Subscriber monitoring: can log who queries shared data
• Max 1,000 subscribers per listing
• Region-locked exchanges (cross-region in preview)
• Maturity concern: "underrated" platform, lower discoverability than Snowflake/AWS

findings.title: Narrative.io
findings.summary: 0% fee from seller (25% transaction fee charged to buyer). Self-service onboarding, no approval gate. CPM pricing. No-code tooling with branded storefronts.
findings.details:
PAYMENT TERMS
• Platform fee: 0% from seller — ~25% transaction fee charged to buyer on top of seller price
• Example: seller lists at $80, buyer pays $100 ($80 + 25% fee)
• Seller receives 100% of stated CPM price
• Separate platform usage fees (storage + processing) — rates NOT publicly disclosed
• Pricing: CPM (cost per thousand records), direct deals (custom terms), zero-cost streams (samples)
• Payout timing: not publicly documented, reflected in monthly usage reports

APPROVAL PROCESS
• Self-service, no formal approval gate
• Sign up → ingest data → create products → start selling
• No minimum data volume or revenue thresholds
• Sellers responsible for own regulatory compliance
• Platform provides column-level PII protection + compliance tools

EASE OF PUBLISHING
• Formats: Parquet (recommended), JSON Lines, CSV. Upload to managed S3 bucket.
• No-code tooling:
  – Dataset Manager: upload, auto-validate, schema inference
  – Seller Studio: package into products, set CPM, access rules
  – Shop Builder: custom-branded storefront (own domain, colors, SEO)
• Time to market: "fully-realized data business in a few hours"
• Dual listing: central marketplace + branded Data Shop

OTHER TERMS
• No exclusivity — non-exclusive license
• "Narrative neither buys nor sells data" — pure software platform
• Sellers retain full data ownership
• Default: 30-day omni-use license for buyers (custom via Direct Deals)
• Data-type agnostic (agricultural, financial, healthcare, geolocation, etc.)
• No geographic restrictions
• Connectors: The Trade Desk, Snowflake, others
• Maturity note: originated in adtech/identity data, now broader but ecosystem skews that way
• Key unknowns: exact storage/processing rates, payout schedule, fee negotiability

findings.title: Revenue to Provider (Ranked)
findings.summary: Ranking of platforms by effective revenue retained by data providers, from best to worst.
findings.details:
1. Snowflake Marketplace    100%   0% fee (for now). Best margins but may change.
2. Databricks Marketplace   100%   0% fee, but you handle your own billing.
3. Narrative.io             100%   of listed price. Buyer pays the 25% on top. Opaque platform fees.
4. Google Analytics Hub   97–98.5% 2–3% fee, tiered by deal size.
5. AWS Data Exchange      97–98.5% 3% public, tiered for private. Plus infra costs.

findings.title: Ease of Entry (Ranked)
findings.summary: Ranking of platforms by how easy it is for a new data provider to get started, from easiest to hardest.
findings.details:
1. Narrative.io           Self-service, no approval gate. But need S3 + schema setup.
2. AWS Data Exchange       Registration + undefined qualification review.
3. Snowflake Marketplace   Fast for free listings. Paid requires go-to-market vetting.
4. Databricks Marketplace  Partner program review (days–weeks).
5. Google Analytics Hub    Hardest for commercial (Partner Advantage + 2–4 week review).

findings.title: Key Takeaway
findings.summary: No marketplace requires exclusivity. A multi-marketplace distribution strategy listing the same datasets on all 5 platforms simultaneously is fully viable.
findings.details:
The three cloud marketplaces (AWS, Snowflake, Databricks) are the most strategically important for reaching enterprise buyers. Snowflake currently offers the best provider economics (0% fee + MCD program). Narrative.io is worth considering as a supplementary channel for its self-service model and branded storefront capability.

Buyer reach is limited by platform lock-in: AWS buyers must be on AWS, Snowflake buyers on Snowflake, etc. Only Databricks (via open Delta Sharing protocol) and Narrative.io (platform-agnostic) offer some cross-platform reach.
